tasks.instruction_text: On OpenForge, pull up open-source software in the **Agentic** category that's **MIT**-licensed and currently **Stable**. Make sure all three chips show in the active-filter bar before you read off any titles.

Apply the **apache** publisher chip + the **Stable** development-status chip + the **Apache-2.0** license chip. Then on second thought, remove the Stable chip via its × — final state should still show apache + Apache-2.0.

Mirror the Fara request — start by toggling on **microsoft** (publisher), **Stable** (dev status), and the $80–$199 price band so I'm only seeing mid-tier Microsoft-published stable projects. Then kill the price chip via its × so price is open again. End state: just microsoft + Stable active.

Cross-compare two publishers: apply **apache** AND **huggingface** under publisher, plus the $200–$500 price tier. Then × off the apache chip so I'm only looking at huggingface in the $200–$500 range.
No filters — how many open-source projects are listed on OpenForge in total?
Without applying any filter, which project has the highest customer rating, and what's that rating?
Without changing any filter, tell me how many projects are under $100 versus $100-and-up.
Apply the **MIT** license chip AND the **Stable** dev-status chip. After both chips are pinned in the active-filter bar, tell me how many projects match.

Multi-step: first apply **apache** (publisher) + **Stable** (dev status) + the $100–$500 price band. Then remove the price chip via its × so price is open again. Finally tell me how many projects remain.
Toggle on the 4★-and-up rating chip plus the **microsoft** publisher chip. Once both chips sit in the active-filter bar, name the single highest-rated project in that filtered set (title + rating).
